name: acts
description: Acts kernel proof (notes/2026-07-21-acts-projection-model.md): schema-validated acts on a room's sequenced log as the one authoritative record of coordination state, with every work surface derived as a projection fold. Ships the $acts emission feature, the $projection base class, the $case room, and the $task_board proof projection.

features.description: Stateless feature carrying the internal act-emission primitive. Mounted on a $case (or any $space subclass that adopts the kernel), its effective surface is <space>:act. Emission requires a sequenced turn on the consumer's own log and an internal caller; payloads validate against event_schema; attached projections fold in the same turn, fail-closed.

verbs.name: can_be_attached_by
act
_validate_payload

classes.description: Base class for act projections (acts kernel S2.3): consumes + fold + rows + view. rows/consumes/row_cap/at_seq are perms-empty so only catalog-author verbs write them — the fold is the sole writer of coordination rows. A projection lives in its room's anchor cluster so fold writes share the turn's atomicity.

verbs.name: fold
view
view_row
rebuild_from

classes.description: The Tasks proof projection (S5): coordination state only — no artifact names, no holder, no timestamps. view_row joins name and the lease at view time; times resolve from row seqs via the log.

verbs.name: fold
view_row

classes.description: Second-surface proof projection (acts kernel S8.2 tier B3): one row per task kind with counts of tasks in each state - { kind, open, claimed, closed }. Folds the same recorded tasks.* acts as the board with zero domain-verb edits and zero edits to existing folds. task_states is the fold-private per-task index (kind + live state) needed because claim/release/close payloads carry no kind and close does not say whether the task was held.

verbs.name: fold

classes.description: A room whose work is recorded as acts on its own sequenced log (case = room, 2026-07-12 gravity model; content model = acts kernel). Domain verbs validate against board rows, apply physical effects, and emit acts in the same turn. The journal is a paged log read.
